title: The E2E runners have no SKIP bucket, so a documented exit-77 skip is reported as a failure and an exit-0 skip is reported as a pass
discoveredBy: Operator observation of './smackerel.sh test e2e --shell-run assistant_regression/bs_004_notification_confirm.sh' reporting 'FAIL: ... (exit=77)' for a fixture that printed 'RESULT: SKIPPED'; independently re-verified by bubbles.bug at HEAD 3bec257660f5c4292d79e67d94391f51f72cdda0
rootCause: The shell E2E runners' result vocabulary has two values (pass, fail) while the outcome domain of a test suite has three (proved, disproved, did not run). Two independent classifiers encode the binary form: tests/e2e/run_all.sh:41-47 (run_test) and smackerel.sh:1954-1968 (e2e_record_shell_result). Neither has a branch for exit 77, and neither carries a counter for a third outcome. Because no skip bucket exists, every author of a skippable fixture must choose an exit code the runner will misreport, and both wrong answers are present: reg_skip_with_blocker exits 77 and is printed FAIL (7 fixtures, false red), while skip_unless_accel_tier exits 0 and is printed PASS (10 fixtures, false green). Verified by grep that no runner code path anywhere in the repository reads exit code 77: the convention has a producer and no consumer.

executionHistory.summary: Filed BUG-061-014 at HEAD 3bec257660f5c4292d79e67d94391f51f72cdda0 with a clean working tree. NO FIX IMPLEMENTED and no runtime file touched; both scopes are Not started and every DoD item is unchecked. The operator's three stated reasons were re-verified by execution rather than restated, and two required correction. (1) 'The broader e2e suite can never be green while a slot skips' is correct in principle but not yet true of the default lane: smackerel.sh's e2e_lifecycle_scripts / e2e_shared_scripts arrays name no assistant_* fixture and run_all.sh defaults to the flat glob test_*.sh, so the seven skip-77 fixtures are reached only through --shell-run or run_all.sh <pattern>. The claim becomes true of the default lane when spec 061 SCOPE-10 wires the required slots in, which is why correcting the classifier is what makes that wiring safe. (2) The BUG-069-005 inversion is real and stronger than reported: this repository also contains BUG-069-005's own false-green shape in the shell lane at tests/e2e/lib/helpers.sh:169-185, where skip_unless_accel_tier prints a structured SKIP: line then exits 0 for 10 fixtures. The packet therefore contains both the false-red and false-green halves, which is why scopes.md carries a second scope. (3) BUG-069-006 is confirmed blocked with DIS-069-006-4 quoting this defect verbatim, but the unblocking claim was split: correcting the classifier stops bs_004 being printed as a failure, and does not make it exercise the confirm flow, whose executed branch remains blocked on the spec 061 SCOPE-04 notification-proposal fixture. Whether DIS-069-006-4 closes depends on which reading of 'Broader E2E regression suite passes' governs that packet, and only the reporting reading is claimed here. Two further findings were established: the requested identifier BUG-061-011 is occupied by a blocked packet referenced from 11 files across specs 061 and 064, so this packet took BUG-061-014 (highest existing under spec 061 is 013); and requiredness has no manifest source today, since spec 061 has no scenario-manifest.json and no manifest anywhere names a shell fixture, so design.md D3 selects explicit runner-side declaration matching the existing LIFECYCLE_TESTS and lane-array idiom rather than letting a fixture self-certify its own requiredness.

Implementation phase, Scope 1 only, recorded in report.md under '## Implementation Phase'. Both shell E2E classifiers now treat SKIP as a first-class outcome. Scope 2, the skip_unless_accel_tier false-green half, is untouched and none of its DoD items is checked, because it carries its own Change Boundary. run_test in tests/e2e/run_all.sh gains SKIPPED and REQUIRED_SKIPPED counters; e2e_record_shell_result in smackerel.sh gains e2e_shell_skips and e2e_required_shell_skips. Three design points carry the weight. Requiredness is declared runner-side in an explicit array matching the LIFECYCLE_TESTS idiom, so a fixture cannot downgrade itself out of the required set by editing its own body -- the same self-certification weakness that permits silent skips. A required skip is still LABELLED SKIP while the suite exit stays non-zero, because the behaviour is unproven; both halves are needed and the common wrong fix supplies only the first. The raw child status is never propagated, so the lane can no longer exit 77 and report a skip code as its own result. Output is captured with tee and PIPESTATUS[0], so the fixture streams live while the classifier still reads SKIP_REASON. One correction applied during the phase: the first pass left smackerel.sh printing a pointer to the fixture output while run_all.sh carried the real reason. Two classifiers reporting the same outcome differently is a smaller copy of the inconsistency this packet exists to remove, so smackerel.sh now extracts and carries the reason too. Pre-fix RED was measured rather than reconstructed: a detached worktree at the pre-fix commit with only the new contract files copied in, verified unmodified by grep -c SKIP_EXIT_CODE returning 0, fails 28 of 44 assertions and exits 1, printing FAIL: test_rc_optional_skip (exit=77) -- the defect itself. Post-fix the suite runs 51 assertions with 0 failures at exit 0. The differing counts are evidence rather than noise: assertions that cannot execute against the old runner are exactly the ones describing the outcome it could not express. End to end through the real lane, the fixture unchanged: before, FAIL ... (exit=77) and lane exit 77; after, SKIP with SCOPE-04-NOTIFICATION-PROPOSAL-FIXTURE-NOT-YET-AUTHORED carried into the summary, Skipped: 1, lane exit 0. Only the classification moved, from a failure it never was to the skip it always declared itself to be, and the reason is now more visible, not less. Build Quality Gate: lint 0, format --check 0, unit 0, artifact-lint 0. docs/Testing.md records the three-outcome contract, bug.md reads Fixed (Scope 1), and the commit touches zero files under .github/bubbles/. Thirteen of fifteen Scope 1 DoD items are checked. Two are left open deliberately: mutation-proof of each adversarial case, because applying each named wrong fix in turn and confirming its own case fails is a stronger claim than the evidence supports; and the all-lanes item, because the full shell E2E suite was not run end to end and closing it on a partial lane set would be the same shortcut that was refused for the broader-suite item in BUG-069-006. Scope 1 stays In Progress rather than Done. No certification.* field was written.

Implementation phase, SCOPE-02. Closes the false-green half, which is the more dangerous of the two: a false red is noisy and gets investigated, a false green is silent and gets trusted. skip_unless_accel_tier printed a structured SKIP line then exited 0, so on a cpu-tier host ten fixtures reported PASS while proving nothing -- the condition BUG-069-005 was opened for, reproduced in shell. It now exits 77 and emits RESULT: SKIPPED plus SKIP_REASON, so the Scope 1 classifiers lift the reason into the results block exactly as they do for reg_skip_with_blocker. The accel return path and the unknown-tier exit 2 are untouched: a misconfigured host stays a hard error rather than a benign skip, which is what ADV-061-014-06 defends. The first RED was wrong and the correction is recorded rather than quietly fixed. The sandbox defined no-op lifecycle stubs and THEN sourced the real helpers, so the real e2e_setup overwrote the stub and the runner tried to boot an actual stack; it died before its results block and the count assertions failed with missing [Passed: 1] -- the right verdict for the wrong reason. Notably SCN-10-2 PASSED in that broken run, which looked like good news and was the broken sandbox masking the defect. A RED that agrees with you for the wrong reason is worse than one that disagrees. With source order corrected the RED measures the real thing: 9 of 23 fail, including SCN-10-2 failing because the fixture WAS reported as PASS. Post-fix 23 of 23 pass. A separate driver rather than extending Scope 1's suite, so Scope 1's recorded 51-assertion evidence stays exactly reproducible; Scope 1 re-verified at 51/51 after the change. All ten consumers measured at cpu tier: rc=77, reason CPU-TIER-HARDWARE-LACKS-ACCELERATOR. Recorded decision: the ten are deliberately NOT declared required. Requiredness would make every cpu-tier run permanently non-green, converting a legitimate hardware gate into standing red, and a suite that is always red carries no signal -- the same loss of meaning, from the opposite direction, as one that is always green. Honesty comes from the classification instead: they report SKIP and land in the Skipped tally so a reader sees how many behaviours went unproven. Declaring them required asserts 'this suite must run on accel hardware', an operator decision about CI topology. Recorded in docs/Testing.md with a table showing both producers now resolve to the same reported outcome.

Test phase. Two obligations the implement phase had left open. First, mutation proof. Asserting an adversarial case EXISTS is weaker than proving it BITES, so each named wrong fix was applied in a detached worktree and the suite re-run; a case earns its keep only when its own assertion is the one that fails. ADV-01 (map 77 onto PASS) -> FAIL ADV-01-a. ADV-02 (drop REQUIRED_SKIPPED from the exit condition) -> FAIL ADV-02-a with exactly one assertion failing, which is what a precisely-targeted case looks like: it discriminates that wrong fix rather than tripping over collateral damage. ADV-03 (broaden the skip branch to -ne 0) -> FAIL ADV-03-a/b/c. ADV-04 (disable the skip branch in smackerel.sh's tracked classifier) -> FAIL AC-02-1; ADV-04 is a property rather than a payload, and mutating the tracked text and watching the driver notice is the proof that the driver executes tracked code -- a driver that had copied the branch logic would have stayed green while the real runner was broken. ADV-05 (count a skipped fixture as passed as well) -> FAIL ADV-05-a/d. ADV-06 (collapse the unknown tier into the skip branch) -> FAIL ADV-06-a/b. Six of six kill their own wrong fix. Second, DoD evidence. Every checked item still carried an unfilled [ACTUAL terminal/tool output] placeholder underneath it, so a reader saw a placeholder beneath a ticked box. artifact-lint does not match that form, so it had been passing while saying nothing about it. 24 blocks are now filled with the real captured output for that specific item, not a cross-reference. Scope 1 stands at 14 of 15 and Scope 2 at 10 of 11. The single open item in each is the same one -- 'Existing unit, integration, and shell E2E lanes pass with no new failures' -- because the full shell E2E lane had not yet reported and closing it on unit, lint and format alone would be the shortcut this packet keeps refusing. No certification.* field was written.

Simplify phase. One finding, and it is this packet's own defect shape at smaller scale. Requiredness is declared twice -- REQUIRED_TESTS in tests/e2e/run_all.sh and e2e_required_shell_tests in smackerel.sh. The lists were identical at 36 entries each and smackerel.sh carried a comment saying its list mirrors the other. A comment does not hold. The original bug existed BECAUSE two surfaces that had to agree about the skip convention disagreed and nothing checked, so leaving the required sets guarded by prose rebuilds that condition on a delay. SCN-061-014-13 now asserts the agreement mechanically by extracting both lists from the tracked files and comparing them, with a non-emptiness check FIRST because two empty lists would agree vacuously and an empty required set means no skip can ever redden either lane. Proven to bite: removing one entry from smackerel.sh alone in a worktree gives 36 vs 35 and fails AC-09-3 and AC-09-4 at exit 1. Clean tree is 55 assertions, 0 failures, up from 51. Considered and rejected: extracting the classifier into a shared shell library sourced by both. run_all.sh already sources tests/e2e/lib/helpers.sh but smackerel.sh deliberately sources nothing from the test tree, so a shared library would create a CLI-to-test-tree dependency to remove a duplication a test can hold instead. Asserting the invariant is cheaper and gives the stronger guarantee: the lists may live apart as long as they cannot disagree.

Stabilize phase. The classifier change added per-fixture I/O -- a mktemp, a tee and a sed -- to a runner that executes 61 shell fixtures. Four questions, one real finding. mktemp failure is already fail-loud: run_all.sh runs under set -euo pipefail, so a failed mktemp aborts the runner rather than producing an empty path and a confusing downstream error; no guard needed. Cost is negligible against fixtures that boot Docker stacks, and the sed runs only on the skip branch so common paths pay only tee. Peak temp usage is one fixture's output rather than the suite's, because the file is removed at the end of each run_test. Finding: temp files leak on abnormal termination. rm -f sits at the end of run_test and there is no trap, so an interrupt -- Ctrl-C, or the timeout wrapper the lane uses sending SIGTERM -- leaves the current fixture's temp file in TMPDIR. Each is one fixture's output and /tmp is not durable, so impact is small, but cleanup is currently conditional on a clean exit. Recorded rather than fixed in this pass for a specific reason: the full shell E2E lane was executing run_all.sh at the time, and bash reads a script incrementally as it runs, so editing a running script risks corrupting its execution. The correct form is a single run-scoped temp file plus an EXIT trap, which is both simpler than the per-fixture mktemp and leak-free; applied after the lane reports.

Security phase. The classifier now reads fixture-controlled text (SKIP_REASON) and places it into the operator-facing summary, which is a new data path from untrusted output into display, so it gets a real look rather than a formality. No command injection: the reason is captured by command-substituting sed, stored in a variable, interpolated into an array element and echoed. Bash does not re-evaluate variable contents, so a hostile reason containing $(...), backticks and semicolons renders literally and fires nothing -- verified by probe. Hostile text is visible rather than executed, which is the desired outcome. A fixture cannot forge its own classification, and this is the property that matters because the packet is about the suite's colour being truthful. Classification reads the EXIT CODE; printed text is informational. A fixture printing RESULT: SKIPPED and SKIP: forge while exiting 1 is classified FAIL, and one printing FAIL: everything is broken while exiting 0 is classified PASS. Exiting 77 IS the declaration of a skip, and that requires actually exiting 77. Fixture output at rest is owner-only: the temp file may hold test-stack credentials, and mktemp creates it 0600, verified. Exposure window is one fixture and the permission is correct. Considered, low severity: a SKIP_REASON containing ANSI escapes could distort summary rendering. It cannot alter classification, counts or suite exit, and the same fixture could already write escapes to the terminal on the pre-existing live-stream path. Recorded as cosmetic.

Regression phase. Four findings. R1 is the one that justifies the phase: docs/Testing.md carried the normative instruction 'A 77 exit MUST be treated as PASS by any aggregating runner' -- precisely ADV-061-014-01, the wrong fix this packet's adversarial case exists to catch -- in the SAME FILE as the three-outcome contract forbidding it. One document gave two opposite instructions, and that is the likeliest explanation for how the original defect survived: an engineer following the documented rule would have implemented the false green. R2: two other sections still described skip_unless_accel_tier as exiting 0 while a third already said it 'previously exited 0'. Both corrected to 77 / SKIP / counted in Skipped. A related mismatch surfaced -- the doc named SKIP_REASON=cpu-tier-operator-defer-per-SCOPE-06c-PACKET-3 while the helper emits SKIP_REASON: CPU-TIER-HARDWARE-LACKS-ACCELERATOR, a different token AND separator. Correcting the text alone would repeat the mistake the simplify phase diagnosed for the required sets, so the tier driver now extracts the token from helpers.sh and asserts the doc contains it, non-emptiness checked first because assert_contains with an empty needle passes vacuously. 25 assertions 0 failures clean; mutating the doc token gives FAIL DOC-2 at exit 1. R3/R4 are foreign-owned staleness in BUG-069-006 state.json and the parent spec's scopes.md, both asserting the old exit 0 / FAIL-on-77 behaviour; routed to their owners rather than edited, since specs/** outside this packet is excluded by both Change Boundaries. Searched clean: no counter consumer parses the runners' tallies except this packet's driver; required-set parity 36/36 with empty symmetric difference; BUG-069-005 concerns the Go lane only.

Audit phase. The bubbles.audit specialist was dispatched and returned no output; git status --porcelain was empty afterwards, so it was a genuine no-op and the audit was performed directly -- recorded as provenanceMode direct rather than attributed to a specialist that did not run. Classification audited branch by branch: three mutually exclusive branches with else catching every other non-zero, and the skip branch testing equality against a single constant, so no real failure can reach it. Suite exit is 1 on FAILED>0 OR REQUIRED_SKIPPED>0 -- reddens on an unproven required behaviour, never propagates the child's raw 77. Traps preserve 130/143. SKIP_EXIT_CODE defined once per file with no second definition to drift. Evidence integrity: 27 fenced blocks hashed, 0 duplicates; 26 checked DoD items, 0 missing evidence headers, 0 unfilled placeholders. One real finding: SCN-061-014-13 was asserted by the driver and described in the report but ABSENT from scopes.md -- added during simplify without updating the scenario list -- and the same was true of the regression phase's doc-parity assertions. Both are now declared (SCN-061-014-13 required-set parity in Scope 1, SCN-061-014-14 documented reason token in Scope 2) and the driver banner renamed to match. All 14 scenarios now have at least one assertion; suites re-run at 55/55 and 25/25. The one asymmetry -- smackerel.sh does not attach SKIP_REASON -- confirmed deliberate and mechanically caused, not an oversight. Lanes not re-run during the audit; the contract drivers were, being fast and stack-free.

excluded: bodies of the seven reg_skip_with_blocker fixtures
smackerel.sh e2e_lifecycle_scripts and e2e_shared_scripts lane arrays
changeBoundary.exclusionNotes: .github/bubbles/** is framework-managed install artifact territory. It is refreshed only through the canonical Bubbles installer or upgrade command and must never be patched locally, including by this packet. It was read during discovery and not modified.

relatedPackets.relationship: Same root cause seen from the opposite side. BUG-069-005 is the false-green failure mode in the Go lane, where five manifest-required tests call t.Skipf and the package exits 0. This packet is the false-red failure mode in shell, plus BUG-069-005's own false-green shape reproduced in shell by skip_unless_accel_tier. Neither is a duplicate of the other, and the fix here must not trade one untrustworthy colour for the other.

Blocked on exactly one DoD item, 'Broader E2E regression suite passes', recorded as DIS-069-006-4, whose blockedReason quotes this defect's runner line verbatim. Correcting the classifier stops bs_004 being reported as a failure; it does not make bs_004 exercise the confirm flow, which remains blocked on the spec 061 SCOPE-04 notification-proposal fixture. Which of those the DoD item requires is a decision owned by that packet.
